Question: What pre-built connectors exist for HR systems (Workday, etc.) and Finance systems (Workday, Maconomy, Dynamics F&O, etc.)? Describe depth of integration.
Response: Enterprise system integrations are exposed as MCP servers governed through APIM AI Gateway. Each MCP server provides typed tool definitions that GHCP SDK sessions (inside MAF agent executors) discover and invoke. For POC1 (Finance): Workday MCP server (SAML-bridged via Okta for HR/finance data), Dynamics 365 F&O native connector, Maconomy REST adapter wrapped as MCP server. For POC2 (HR): Greenhouse ATS MCP server (API App Credentials), LinkedIn Recruiter MCP server (OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code), Workday MCP server (hiring data), Microsoft Graph MCP server (calendar/email via OBO flow), ServiceNow MCP server (IT provisioning). All MCP servers route through APIM AI Gateway which handles auth injection, rate limiting, content safety, and discovery. Depth of integration is full read-write: agents parse data, validate, and write back through the same MCP interface with business rule enforcement in the skill layer.
Key Technologies: MCP Servers, APIM AI Gateway, Okta/Entra federation

Question: Describe your API and webhook support. Provide documentation for REST/SOAP APIs, webhooks, and SDKs for custom integrations.
Response: Four integration patterns available. (1) MCP servers (pro-code): any REST/OpenAPI endpoint can be wrapped as an MCP server with typed tool definitions, auth injection, and parameter mapping. APIM AI Gateway provides a REST-to-MCP gateway that auto-generates MCP tool definitions from OpenAPI specs. (2) Logic Apps (low-code MCP): citizen developers chain together 1,400+ prebuilt connectors (SharePoint, Outlook, Dataverse, SAP, ServiceNow, etc.) and the Logic App is exposed as an MCP tool via APIM REST-to-MCP gateway — no Python required. Governed identically to hand-written MCP servers. (3) Webhooks: Azure Durable Functions exposes HTTP endpoints for event-driven triggering. External systems fire webhooks that trigger new workflow phases or raise events on waiting orchestrations. (4) SDKs: GHCP SDK (Python, TypeScript) for the agent executor runtime and MCP servers; Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF, Python/.NET) for authoring workflow graphs of typed executors. Azure SDKs for all Azure services. M365 Agents SDK for publishing agents to Teams/Copilot surfaces. All APIs are documented on Microsoft Learn and GitHub. Custom MCP servers follow the open MCP specification.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK (Python/TypeScript), Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) v1.0, MCP protocol, APIM REST-to-MCP gateway, Azure Logic Apps (low-code MCP), Azure Durable Functions webhooks
POC Demo: POC1: Show custom Maconomy MCP server built from REST API spec using APIM gateway.

Question: How do agents perform secure write-back to source systems? Describe validation, business rule enforcement, and error handling for write operations.
Response: Write-back is governed at four structural levels — "deterministic by default, agentic by exception". (1) Skill-level validation: each skill defines business rules (three-way match for invoice validation, comp band checks for offer letters). The agent executor (GHCP SDK session) reasons about validation before attempting writes. (2) MAF validator executor: downstream of the agent executor node, a validator enforces schema/policy constraints on typed output before it reaches any write executor — judge/executor separation as an explicit graph edge. (3) Hook-level enforcement: GHCP SDK session hooks (`onPreToolUse`) intercept write operations inside the session. Non-revocable actions (send email, submit payment, extend offer) are blocked and routed to the human's PA for approval. After approval, execution is deterministic — no LLM in the write path. (4) APIM-level governance: all MCP tool calls route through APIM AI Gateway which enforces auth, rate limiting and content safety. Error handling: MCP servers return typed errors the agent executor can reason about; MAF validator executors catch policy failures; Durable Functions provides retry with backoff at phase level. Failed writes logged to the action ledger.
Key Technologies: GHCP SDK hooks (onPreToolUse/onPostToolUse), Microsoft Agent Framework (MAF) validator executors, APIM AI Gateway policies, Azure Durable Functions retry
POC Demo: POC1: Demonstrate high-value invoice approval gate — agent prepares payment, hook blocks execution, routes to Finance BP for approval, deterministic execution after approval.

Question: Does the platform include integration middleware or ESB capabilities for managing complex data flows between agents and enterprise systems?
Response: APIM AI Gateway serves as the central integration middleware for all agent-to-system communication. It manages: model routing (load balancing, failover, token limits), MCP tool governance (auth, rate limiting, content safety, discovery), A2A agent mediation (agent card registration, policy enforcement), and skill lifecycle management (via Azure API Center). For complex data flows requiring transformation or orchestration beyond what MCP servers provide, Azure Durable Functions handles multi-step data coordination (e.g. invoice data from Workday enriched with D365 F&O data before routing). Event Grid provides event-driven integration between systems. This is not a traditional ESB — it is a purpose-built AI gateway that governs all interactions between agents and enterprise systems.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway, Azure Event Grid, Azure Durable Functions

Question: Describe your data security model: encryption (at rest, in transit), access control (RBAC, ABAC), and MFA support.
Response: Encryption: all data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS 1.2+) across all Azure services. Workflow state in Cosmos DB uses service-managed or customer-managed encryption keys. Access control: Entra Agent ID provides RBAC on Hosted Agent containers — each domain agent (Hiring Agent, Finance Agent, Fleet Manager) has scoped permissions to only its required tools and data. ABAC enforcement at the tool-call level via APIM policies. Human access to Control Plane UI governed by Entra RBAC with role-based views (HR BP sees hiring workflows, Finance BP sees budget gates). OBO flows ensure human-triggered actions carry the human's delegated permissions for audit attribution. MFA: enforced via Entra Conditional Access policies on both human and agent identities. Okta federation via Entra External ID for SAML-bridged access to business systems.
Key Technologies: Microsoft Entra ID, Entra Agent ID, APIM policies, Cosmos DB encryption, Okta federation
POC Demo: POC2: Show role-based Control Plane views — HR BP and Finance BP see different filtered dashboards based on Entra RBAC.

Question: What data loss prevention features exist to control data access and exfiltration by agents?
Response: DLP is enforced at three layers. (1) Foundry Guardrails: intercept tool calls and responses at four intervention points (input, output, tool-call, tool-response). PII detection blocks sensitive data in agent outputs. Content safety policies prevent inappropriate content. Task Adherence guardrail detects drift from the agent's defined purpose. (2) APIM AI Gateway: content filtering policies on all MCP tool calls. Token rate limiting prevents excessive data retrieval. All requests logged for audit. (3) Microsoft Purview: DLP policies extend to agent interactions — data classification labels flow through the system. Defender provides threat detection for anomalous agent behaviour (unusual data access patterns, jailbreak attempts, prompt injection). Agent-scoped permissions via Entra ensure each Hosted Agent can only access its domain's data — the Hiring Agent cannot read finance data and vice versa.
Key Technologies: Foundry Guardrails, APIM content safety, Microsoft Purview DLP, Microsoft Defender
POC Demo: POC2: Demonstrate Foundry Guardrails blocking PII in agent output — candidate SSN detected and redacted before surfacing to Control Plane.

Question: What data residency and sovereignty controls are available? Describe regional deployment options.
Response: Data residency enforced at the platform level, not developer-configured. APIM AI Gateway provides jurisdiction-based model routing: a workflow carrying jurisdiction=DE routes model inference exclusively to EU-hosted endpoints. Candidate PII from a German hire cannot reach US-hosted model endpoints. Cosmos DB supports multi-region deployment with data residency controls per region. Azure has 60+ regions globally for regional deployment. Foundry Hosted Agents deploy to specified Azure regions. Audit logs in Azure Log Analytics support region-specific retention. Jurisdiction context flows through the entire stack: workflow state carries jurisdiction metadata, APIM routing policies enforce region constraints, Foundry Guardrails enforce PII rules universally, and jurisdiction-specific skills load automatically based on workflow context.
Key Technologies: APIM AI Gateway jurisdiction routing, Azure regions, Cosmos DB regional deployment
POC Demo: POC2 Appendix B: Demonstrate identical workflow for USA vs Germany hire — show APIM routing German candidate data exclusively to EU model endpoints.

Question: Describe version control and rollback capabilities for agents and workflows. What approval gates exist before promotion?
Response: All agent artefacts are version-controlled in Git. Skills (SKILL.md files) are registered in Azure API Center with lifecycle management: Design -> Preview -> Production -> Deprecated. Promotion between stages requires approval gates. APIM policies are version-controlled via APIOps CI/CD pipelines with PR review gates. Governance policy changes (autonomy thresholds, compliance rules) require PR review with author, timestamp, and rationale. Durable Functions workflow definitions are deployed via standard CI/CD (Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions) with environment-specific configuration (dev/staging/production). Rollback: API Center supports reverting skills to previous versions. APIM supports instant policy rollback. Durable Functions supports deployment slot rollback. Workflow state in Cosmos DB supports point-in-time restore. The full dev/test/staging/production lifecycle is managed through CI/CD with approval gates at each promotion boundary.
Key Technologies: Azure API Center, APIOps CI/CD, Git, Azure DevOps/GitHub Actions
POC Demo: POC1: Show skill promotion from Design to Production in API Center with approval gate.
